holidays.name: King Tut Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the boy pharaoh and the golden treasures that made the world fall in love with ancient Egypt. Break out the eyeliner, drape yourself in gold, and walk like an Egyptian.
holidays.origin: It marks November 4, 1922. On that day, a team led by archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the first step leading down to the tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
holidays.funFact: Tutankhamun became pharaoh at about age nine, and his tomb was one of the best-preserved royal burials ever found. It held more than 5,000 objects, including a solid gold funerary mask.

holidays.name: National Candy Day
holidays.description: A sugar-fueled holiday that invites you to raid the candy bowl, share treats with friends, and revisit the sweets of your childhood. It lands just after Halloween, which makes for a convenient leftover loot situation.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and it has become a favorite of candy fans and confectioners.
holidays.funFact: Americans buy billions of dollars' worth of candy every year, and a big share of that happens around Halloween. National Candy Day is a good excuse to finish what's left.

holidays.name: Use Your Common Sense Day
holidays.description: A gentle, tongue-in-cheek reminder to pause, think things through, and avoid doing silly things. Skip the shortcuts, read the instructions, and maybe don't microwave that.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and it spreads mostly through its own cheeky message.
holidays.funFact: Many warning labels exist because someone, somewhere, did something surprising. Using your common sense saves you from becoming the reason for the next one.
